newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FIVE-WAY TIE FOR LEAD AT U.S. SENIOR OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FIVE-WAY TIE FOR LEAD AT U.S. SENIOR OPEN.

text.p: Tom Wargo birdied the last two holes Thursday to join a five-way tie for the lead after the opening round of the $1.3 million U.S. Senior Open, the third of four majors on the Senior Tour.
Wargo, whose first Senior Tour victory came at the 1993 PGA Seniors' Championship, overcame back-to-back bogeys on the back nine to shoot a one-under-par 69.
He was tied with red-hot Gil Morgan, John Bland, Steve Veriato and Kermit Zarley, the only other golfers to break par at the Olympia Fields Country Club.
Dave Eichelberger, who flirted with the lead all day, settled for an even-par 70 and was tied for sixth with Leonard Thompson and Buddy Whitten.

Former champion Larry Laoretti was in a group of 10 golfers two shots back after opening-round 71s. The pack also included Bruce Summerhays, Chi Chi Rodriguez, Bill Hall, Frank Conner, Marion Heck, Bill Tindall, David Oakley, John Jacobs and Dana Quigley.
Defending champion Dave Stockton injured his back Wednesday and struggled to a seven-over 77.
Stockton edged Hale Irwin by two strokes at last year's U.S. Senior Open in Beachwood, Ohio and is trying to become the first repeat champion since Gary Player won back-to-back titles in 1987-88.

Irwin, who won three U.S. Open titles on the PGA Tour and is the leading money-winner on Senior Tour this year, posted a three-over 73. He has won just over $1 million in only 11 events and has four victories, including the PGA Seniors Championship, the year's second major.
Two-time champion Jack Nicklaus carded a 73, two-time winner Gary Player had a 76 and 66-year-old three-time champ Miller Barber posted a 77.

Nicklaus's performance this week will weigh heavily in his decision to compete in next month's British Open. Should he skip the British Open, Nicklaus would end his streak of playing in 142 consecutive major championships.
The par-70 Olympia Fields course measures 6,841 yards. First prize is $232,500 and a win carries with it automatic entry into next year's U.S. Open at the Olympic Club in San Francisco.
